name: focus-vs-click ordering
comment: A focus-in delivered before a click is a refocusing click (handled, no mode change); the byte-identical click without a preceding focus-in changes mode. Only the ordered focus event distinguishes them -- the exact case send-events makes testable.

steps.eval: (progn (defvar my-state "semi-char") (defvar my-focus-pending nil) (setq my-state "semi-char" my-focus-pending nil) (unless (get 'my-focus 'armed) (add-function :after after-focus-change-function (lambda () (setq my-focus-pending t))) (put 'my-focus 'armed t)) (with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create "play") (erase-buffer) (insert "hello world") (goto-char (point-min)) (use-local-map (make-sparse-keymap)) (local-set-key [down-mouse-1] #'ignore) (local-set-key [mouse-1] (lambda (e) (interactive "e") (if my-focus-pending (setq my-focus-pending nil) (setq my-state "copy"))))) (switch-to-buffer "play") t)
steps.comment: fixture: after-focus-change-function arms a 'focus pending' flag; the mouse-1 command keeps semi-char on a focus click but enters copy mode otherwise
focus-in THEN the click, one ordered stream: the focus hook runs before the click command
treated as a focus click -- no mode change
the byte-identical click with NO preceding focus-in
switched to copy mode -- the only difference was the ordered focus event
